```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(repair)
```

`repair_bayes_plugin()` explicitly opts in to **experimental plug-in REPAIR**
using a Bayesian-fitted Gaussian measurement model. The structural estimator
remains modified method of moments. Its standard errors, normal tests and
confidence intervals condition on measurement-parameter summaries. They are not
posterior SDs or credible intervals. Unconditional coverage of the complete,
refitted Bayesian measurement-model workflow has not been established.

## Fit the measurement model, then create a snapshot

The Bayesian packages are optional dependencies. Fit models through their native
interfaces so priors, sampler settings and model assessment remain explicit.
These examples sample models and are not run when building this guide.

```{r rstanarm-example, eval=FALSE}
library(rstanarm)
growth <- rstanarm::stan_lmer(
  Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject), data = lme4::sleepstudy,
  prior = rstanarm::normal(0, 50, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior_intercept = rstanarm::normal(250, 100, autoscale = FALSE),
  prior_aux = rstanarm::exponential(.05, autoscale = FALSE),
  chains = 4, iter = 2000, seed = 42, adapt_delta = .95
)
measurement <- repair_bayes_plugin(growth)  # experimental-inference warning
people <- data.frame(Subject = levels(lme4::sleepstudy$Subject), x = 1:18)
repair_effects(measurement)
fit <- repair(re("Days") ~ x, measurement, people, "Subject")
summary(fit)
repair_coefficients(fit)  # conditional model-based confidence intervals
repair_diagnostics(fit, table = "mlm")
```

The artificial `x` column illustrates the interface, not a substantive analysis.
Choose priors using the response/predictor scales and scientific context; these
example choices are not defaults recommended for every application.

```{r brms-example, eval=FALSE}
growth_brms <- brms::brm(
  Reaction ~ Days + (Days | Subject), data = lme4::sleepstudy,
  family = gaussian(link = "identity"),
  prior = c(brms::prior(normal(0, 50), class = "b"),
    brms::prior(normal(250, 100), class = "Intercept"),
    brms::prior(exponential(.05), class = "sigma"),
    brms::prior(exponential(.05), class = "sd"),
    brms::prior(lkj(2), class = "cor")),
  chains = 4, iter = 2000, seed = 43, control = list(adapt_delta = .95)
)
measurement_brms <- repair_bayes_plugin(growth_brms)
fit_brms <- repair(re("Days") ~ x, measurement_brms, people, "Subject")
```

Priors differ across these engines, including covariance-prior families; their
estimates need not coincide. Unwrapped `brmsfit` and `stanreg` objects are rejected.
A snapshot records its original fit and plug-in quantities; recreate it after
changing the fit.

## Initial support boundary

| Component | Accepted | Excluded |
|---|---|---|
| Engine | Sampled `brms::brm()`, `rstanarm::stan_lmer()` or `stan_glmer()` fits | Variational/optimization fits and other stanreg model families |
| Likelihood | One numeric response, Gaussian identity link | Multivariate, non-Gaussian, censored, truncated or measurement-error likelihoods |
| Measurement equation | Additive numeric columns, at least one fixed coefficient | Factors, interactions, inline transformations and special terms; precompute numeric columns instead |
| Random effects | Exactly one ordinary random-effects block and one bare grouping column | Independent multiple blocks, double-bar syntax, nuisance/crossed/nested groups and structured/non-Gaussian random effects |
| Residuals | Constant, independent Gaussian variance | Autocorrelation, heterogeneous/distributional variance and residual extensions |
| Other features | Native effective rows/designs; unused grouping levels omitted by the fitting engine | Weights, offsets, custom Stan code/data, nonlinear models and prior-only fits |
| Sampling information | At least two chains and four retained iterations per chain | Missing posterior/shared-parameter draws or sampler information |
| Structural workflow | Existing additive grammar; random coefficients as predictors, outcomes or both | Bayesian posterior structural inference; Bayesian `repair_refit()` / `repair_bootstrap()` |

The chain/iteration minimum only makes diagnostics computable; it is not an
adequacy criterion. The adapter records Rhat, bulk/tail ESS, mean MCSE,
divergences, maximum observed tree depth and configured-depth hits when available.
It warns for undefined/high Rhat, low ESS, divergences and depth hits; it does not
discard draws or diagnose model adequacy. Resolve sampling problems in the
original fit before interpreting REPAIR. The full audit is available as
`measurement$diagnostics` and `summary(fit)$mlm_models$mlm` (or your model-list
name), including priors and engine version.

Multiple-model analyses retain the existing explicit cross-model error policy.
Separate Bayesian fits do not establish independent measurement errors;
`cross_model_error = "independent"` remains a substantive assumption.

## What is passed to REPAIR

The snapshot uses posterior means of fixed coefficients, complete random
covariance matrices and **squared residual SD draws**:

\[
\widehat\beta=E(\beta\mid y),\qquad
\widehat G=E(G\mid y),\qquad
\widehat\sigma^2=E(\sigma^2\mid y).
\]

It does not square the posterior mean SD or multiply separately averaged SDs
and correlations. From native fitted Gaussian designs it reconstructs

\[
\widetilde b_i=(Z_i^\top\widehat R_i^{-1}Z_i)^{-1}
  Z_i^\top\widehat R_i^{-1}(y_i-X_i\widehat\beta),\qquad
\Psi_i=(Z_i^\top\widehat R_i^{-1}Z_i)^{-1},
\quad\widehat R_i=\widehat\sigma^2 I.
\]

The existing GLS scorer and structural M-MOM estimator are shared with the
frequentist workflows. Scores are deviations from fitted fixed effects, and
full within-person error covariance is retained. The target covariance `G`
is used for plug-in reliability diagnostics, not for these likelihood-only
scores. A proper Bayesian posterior cannot rescue a rank-deficient individual
likelihood design; the usual scoring failure and explicit omission policies apply.

Posterior random-effect SDs are not sampling-error SDs for these scores.
Covariances of marginal MCMC random-effect draws integrate over shared-parameter
uncertainty. Gaussian prior-precision subtraction requires conditional moments
at one matching parameter set. The adapter therefore reconstructs GLS directly.

## Inferential limits and validation

At true fixed shared parameters, Gaussian algebra supplies the additive
sampling-error representation needed by REPAIR. Using estimated shared
parameters introduces an approximation. Conditional structural SEs exclude:

* Uncertainty in fixed effects and residual variance, including dependence
  induced across people by estimating them from the same cohort.
* Prior sensitivity and possible bias from restrictive or misspecified shared
  parameter priors. Removing target shrinkage does not make REPAIR prior-free.
* Measurement-model misspecification and uncertainty in estimated cross-model
  error blocks.

Plug-in reliability also conditions on parameter summaries; it is not a fully
marginalized Bayesian reliability measure. Good sampling diagnostics, high
reliability or successful numerical fitting do not establish structural interval
coverage. Posterior means used as predictors can preserve linear structural
relationships under appropriate calibration conditions; REPAIR is not guaranteed
to improve on that alternative in every setting.

Recomputing REPAIR for posterior parameter draws and pooling coefficients/SEs
does not automatically define a posterior or valid multiple-imputation procedure.
A joint Bayesian structural model or an explicitly specified modular model needs
a separate methodological argument.

Software tests check GLS equivalence and actual native-model extraction. They do
not validate unconditional inference. The development
[full refitted-workflow simulation plan](https://github.com/HallquistLab/repair/blob/51f33760c1f17db227fee48c866503682abdad06/dev/bayesian-plugin-simulation-plan.md)
specifies fresh-data generation and complete Bayesian refitting in every outer
replicate, prior sensitivity, structural estimands, failure accounting,
comparators and coverage/Monte Carlo reporting. No full-workflow coverage results
are claimed by this experimental release.
